At {{height|ft=6|in=3}}, {{convert|200|lb|kg st|abbr=on}}, Murray played as a [[point guard]]–[[shooting guard]]. After attending [[Strawberry Mansion High School]] in Philadelphia, where he starred on the basketball team, he played college basketball for four seasons, first at the [[Meridian Community College]] in [[Meridian, Mississippi]], from 1997 to 1999, and then at [[Shaw University]] located in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], from 2000 to 2002. He is nicknamed "Flip" by childhood friends who often said he looked like [[Bernie Mac]]'s character, "Flip", from the movie ''[[Above The Rim]]''.{{cite news|url=http://www.gainesvilletimes.com/archives/17649/|title=Murray strong sixth man for Hawks|last=Shackleford|first=Rusty|date=2017-01-22|work=Gainesville Times|quote="I don’t know where that came from," Murray said. "My nickname came from the movie ‘Above the Rim."’}} ==Career== Murray was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with pick number 42 in the second round of the [[2002 NBA draft]],{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2002/board/index.html |title=NBA Draft Board |publisher=nba.com |access-date=2011-01-29}} after being [[NCAA]]'s [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] Player of the Year during his senior season at Shaw, as he led the Shaw University Bears to the Division II Final Four in basketball. In his first few NBA seasons he played for the Bucks and for the [[Seattle SuperSonics|SuperSonics]] in [[Seattle]], where he developed as a scoring threat in [[2003-04 NBA season|2003–04]], substituting for [[Ray Allen]] who missed 26 games due to injury, averaging 12 points in 25 minutes, while appearing in all 82 matches. Selected to play in the 2004 [[Rookie Challenge]]. Representing the SuperSonics, Murray scored 25 points and dished out 10 assists for the sophomores.[https://www.nba.com/games/20040213/RKESPH/recap.html Stoudemire Showcases Skills for Sophs] On February 23, 2006, he was traded by Seattle to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Mike Wilks (basketball)|Mike Wilks]] and cash considerations.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/murray_nailon_060223.html |title=Cavaliers Acquire Ronald Murray |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2006-02-23 |access-date=2009-09-26}} In his brief stint with the Cavs, Murray averaged his career-highs in nearly every category. On July 18, 2006, Murray signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]] for $3.6 million over two years, in an effort by the team to improve its bench depth.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/rmurray_signing_060718.html |title=Pistons Sign Guard Ronald "Flip" Murray |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2006-07-18 |access-date=2009-09-26}} In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Murray started eighteen games (twelve in place of point guard [[Chauncey Billups]] and six in place of shooting guard [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]]).{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/DET/2007_start.html | title = 2006-07 Detroit Pistons Starting Lineups | publisher = Basketball-Reference.com | access-date = 2007-07-16}} On February 22, 2008, Murray was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/murray_waived_080222.html |title=Murray Waived |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2008-02-22 |access-date=2009-09-26}} On March 1, he was signed by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. [http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080301/SPORTS/80301004 Pacers Sign Flip Murray] There was an expectation the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] would sign Murray,[https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-cliprep29feb29,1,3590630.story Cassell finally gets his contract buyout] but he elected to go with the Pacers instead.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3273427 Murray signs with Pacers for rest of season], ESPN On August 13, 2008, Murray signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Hawks_Sign_Flip_Murray.html |title=RONALD "Flip" MURRAY SIGNS WITH ATLANTA |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2008-08-13 |access-date=2009-09-26}} On September 25, 2009, the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] signed Murray reportedly to a one-year $1.99 million contract.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_murray_090925.html |title=Bobcats sign free agent combo guard Ronald "Flip" Murray |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-09-25 |access-date=2009-09-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090928101629/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_murray_090925.html |archive-date=2009-09-28 }} On February 18, 2010, Murray was traded in a packaged deal to the [[Chicago Bulls]] for [[Tyrus Thomas]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/thomas_trade_100218.html |title=Bulls receive Murray and Law for Thomas |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-02-18 |access-date=2010-02-18}} Murray's final NBA game was played in Game 5 of the 2010 Eastern Conference First Round against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on April 27, 2010. The Bulls would lose Game 5 to the Cavs 94–96, with Murray recording 6 points and 3 rebounds. Chicago dropped the series to Cleveland 4–1. On January 13, 2011, he signed with the [[Turkey|Turkish]] team [[Efes Pilsen S.K.]] until the end of the 2010–11 season.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/81337/180 Efes Pilsen brings in Flip Murray - Latest - Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL] In October 2012, he signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11035 Grizzlies add Ronald Murray and Kyle Weaver to training camp] but he did not make the team's regular season roster.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11315 Memphis Grizzlies waive Ronald Dupree, Jerome Jordan, Ronald Murray] In January 2013, he signed with the Ukrainian team [[Azovmash Mariupol]].[http://www.bcazovmash.com.ua/en/news_one/1539/ Azovmash adds Murray to the roster] On October 31, 2013, he was reacquired by the Austin Toros of the
